paper.title: MAX on Steroids: A New Measure of Investor Attraction to Lottery Stocks

scope: Replicate the central empirical claims of MAX and the new MAX-beta double-sort anomaly on US CRSP.
rationale: The paper reports fully replicable numerical claims (decile-sort VW means, Newey-West t-stats, alphas under 9 factor models). The headline MAX^beta anomaly is the central contribution, with a clearly stated double-sort methodology and a specific universe filter. The main risks are (a) external factor models (Stambaugh-Yuan SY, Daniel-Hirshleifer-Sun DHS, Baker-Wurgler sentiment) which require CSV ingestion, and (b) the 11-characteristic MIS composite, which requires 11 different Compustat inputs. Both gaps have documented substitutions in data_verification.json. The replication is feasible: CRSP dsf/msf cover 1925-2024, FF factors cover 1926-2025, 13F holdings cover 1980s onward, Compustat annual fundamentals cover the period.

primary_data_required: CRSP daily returns (dsf) and monthly returns (msf)
CRSP PIT universe filter (dsfhdr via shrcd 10/11, exchcd 1/2/3, prc >= $5, SIC exclusion 4900-4949 and 6000-6999)

tables_replicable_candidates: Table 1: Univariate decile sorts on MAX
Table 3: Conditional MAX sorts on MIS
Table 7: Issuance- and MIS-controlled MAX and MAX-beta
Table 9: MAX and MAX-beta by institutional ownership tiers

methodology_notes.max_definition: MAX = average of the 5 highest daily returns within a month (Bali, Cakici, Whitelaw 2011).
methodology_notes.max_beta_construction: First sort stocks into deciles by market beta (BETA). Within each beta decile, sort into deciles by MAX. Group the same MAX decile rank across all 10 beta deciles to form the final MAX-beta decile. Requires at least 15 daily returns per month.
methodology_notes.beta_estimation: OLS slope from regressing daily excess returns on the value-weighted market excess return over a 252-day rolling window.
methodology_notes.factor_models: CAPM, FF3, FFC4, FFCPS, FF5, FF6, FF6PS (the 7-factor), SY (Stambaugh-Yuan 2017), DHS (Daniel-Hirshleifer-Sun 2020).
methodology_notes.newey_west_lags: Six lags for the 1968-2022 sample (paper Eq. 6: 4*(T/100)^{2/9}).
methodology_notes.sample_per_table: Tables 2 and A5 use INST restricted to 1980-04 onward (13F availability); DHS analysis begins 1972-07 per the data sources note.
methodology_notes.decile_assignment: Independent sorts - within each month, by construction.

constraints.stambaugh_yuan_factors: MGMT and PERF are from Robert Stambaugh's website - not in ClickHouse. Documented substitution: drop SY column from per-cell target table, log as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET].
constraints.dhs_factors: FIN and PEAD factors are from Lin Sun's website - not in ClickHouse. Restricted sample July 1972 onward. Documented substitution: drop DHS column, log as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET].
constraints.sentiment_index: Baker-Wurgler monthly sentiment index not in ClickHouse. Not needed for Tables 1, 2, 6 - only used in Table A7 of the paper.

evidence_anchors: MAX definition quote: average of the five highest daily returns generated by a stock in a given month (page 11, sec 3.2)

Sample filter quote: all common stocks (CRSP share codes 10 and 11) traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), American Stock Exchange (Amex), and Nasdaq exchanges from January 1968 to December 2022 (page 11, sec 3.1)
Price filter: We exclude stocks priced below $5 per share (page 12, sec 3.1)
SIC exclusion: utility (SIC codes 4900-4949) and financial (SIC codes 6000-6999) (page 12, sec 3.1)
15-obs rule: at least 15 daily stock return observations (page 12, sec 3.1)

MAX-beta construction: first sort stocks into decile portfolios based on their market beta, then within each beta-sorted portfolio sort again into decile portfolios based on their MAX (page 11, sec 3.2)
